request.title: Werk Süd: both workers on sick leave 12-23 October
request.instructions: Lena Hartmann and Tobias Klein, the two workers of Werk Süd, are on sick leave from 2026-10-12 to 2026-10-23. Keep the orders of Werk Süd on time: check the staffing options (temporary workers, overtime) and ask Cora to adjust the schedule, and Horst to inform customers if something cannot be saved.

## [2026-10-28] task task-01M61BTRXSD6J7W1V1YTC1AFGD | Frame cutter N-CUT-1 in Werk Nord is down
Opened maintenance ticket `MT-001` for `N-CUT-1` and coordinated the ordered response chain.

Reviewed the approved plan against live ERP facts and simulated overtime packages for both factories. No capacity was booked because the packages did not reduce lateness, cost EUR 21,000 per factory, and introduced a new `BEAM-PINE-80` shortage while the existing lateness remained driven by `FOAM-HR35`.

## [2026-10-28] task task-01M61E5E3BR5DWZW3NF1VT4SCW | Werk Süd: both workers on sick leave 12-23 October
Booked 2 temporary workers for F-SOUTH from 2026-10-12 to 2026-10-23 at a cost of EUR 5,200. Cora confirmed the south orders could stay on their existing priorities and Horst did not need to send any customer notices because the ERP showed no broken promises after replanning.

Cora.text:
# Planning autumn bundles can still end late

Rule: A healthy-looking factory queue and material projection do not guarantee that a large unplanned autumn bundle will finish on time; verify the post-change late-order KPI and material-shortage projection before treating the plan as sufficient.

Applies when: Several confirmed but unplanned sales orders are added together during a campaign spike and no extra capacity lever is booked.

Evidence: task `task-a2a-868119cc-9a29-4881-a984-46c0d33a5118`, KPI before `lateOrders=0`, `sofasLate=0`, `unplannedOrders=8` -> after `lateOrders=8`, `sofasLate=970`, `unplannedOrders=0`, `materialShortages={"FOAM-HR35":"production held back from 2026-11-12"}`. Reconfirmed in task `task-a2a-7f936446-e11a-49a9-b9a4-49c7504d3147`, KPI before `lateOrders=0`, `sofasLate=0`, `unplannedOrders=8` -> after `lateOrders=8`, `sofasLate=970`, `unplannedOrders=0`, `materialShortages={"FOAM-HR35":"production held back from 2026-11-11"}`. Reconfirmed again in task `task-a2a-0a7827d1-1a0c-4b1b-a2c9-ebe93ff49b49`, KPI before `lateOrders=0`, `sofasLate=0`, `unplannedOrders=8` -> after `lateOrders=8`, `sofasLate=970`, `unplannedOrders=0`, `materialShortages={"FOAM-HR35":"production held back from 2026-11-12"}`.

# North replan after spindle motor delivery

Rule: When `N-CUT-1` is down for the spindle motor replacement, replan only the North orders that are already late if moving additional work would increase the KPI.

Applies when: A North machine outage is tied to `MT-001` and the required part is already secured with a known arrival date.

Evidence: task `task-a2a-7869e423-a373-4844-a249-0c76c2b9dffa`, KPI before `lateOrders=5`, `sofasLate=520`, `lateOrdersCustomerNotInformed=5` -> after `lateOrders=2`, `sofasLate=220`, `lateOrdersCustomerNotInformed=2`.

- [Log](log.md): append-only session notes for durable company learnings.
- [Planning autumn bundles can still end late](lessons/autumn-bundle-late-even-with-capacity.md): unplanned bundles can still leave all orders late even when current capacity and stock look healthy.
- [North replan after spindle motor delivery](lessons/north-replan-spindle-motor.md): what we learned about re-planning North orders after the spindle motor arrives.
- [Replan Werk Süd after temporary workers were booked](log.md): execution note that the South queue stayed on time and priorities were unchanged.

Replanned the two late North orders `PRD-4200` and `PRD-4202` to `F-SOUTH`, which reduced live KPI from `lateOrders=5`, `sofasLate=520`, `lateOrdersCustomerNotInformed=5` to `lateOrders=2`, `sofasLate=220`, `lateOrdersCustomerNotInformed=2`.
The North machine outage remained in force until `2026-10-13`, so wider replan bundles were rejected in simulation because they increased lateness.

## [2026-10-28] task task-a2a-868119cc-9a29-4881-a984-46c0d33a5118 | Plan unplanned autumn orders SO-2301..SO-2308
Planned eight confirmed but unplanned autumn orders into production without disturbing existing priority-5 work.
The resulting ERP state still showed all eight orders late and introduced a `FOAM-HR35` shortage from `2026-11-12`, so this bundle is not sufficient on its own.

## [2026-10-28] task task-a2a-7f936446-e11a-49a9-b9a4-49c7504d3147 | Execute autumn campaign backlog SO-2301..SO-2308
Created production orders `PRD-4218`..`PRD-4225` for the eight Herbstzauber sales orders without reprioritising existing work.
Live ERP now shows all eight orders planned, but 8 late orders remain and `FOAM-HR35` is projected to hold production back from `2026-11-11`.

## [2026-10-28] task task-a2a-0a7827d1-1a0c-4b1b-a2c9-ebe93ff49b49 | Re-plan Herbstzauber backlog
Replanned the eight Herbstzauber sales orders into production with priority 6, split across both factories and keeping the tier-A orders first in the sequence.
Live ERP still shows 8 late orders and `FOAM-HR35` holding production back from `2026-11-12`, so the backlog remains late after replanning.

Verified the F-SOUTH queue after the staffing change. The seven concerned orders remained on their existing priorities, and the ERP still shows zero late orders for F-SOUTH.

tasks.plan:
# Goal
Keep Werk Süd on time through the sick leave of Lena Hartmann and Tobias Klein from 2026-10-12 to 2026-10-23 by booking the minimum staffing needed for the absence period and preparing the required scheduling and customer follow-ups.

# Inputs
- ERP overview shows F-SOUTH capacity drops from 40 sofas/day on 2026-10-05 to 2026-10-09 to 0 sofas/day from 2026-10-12 through 2026-10-23 because both regular workers are absent.
- Current KPI before action: 7 late orders, 770 sofas late, 7 orders late without customer notice, 0 unplanned orders, 0 material shortages, EUR 0 measure cost.
- F-SOUTH has 7 late production orders today: PRD-4203, PRD-4205, PRD-4207, PRD-4209, PRD-4211, PRD-4213, PRD-4215.
- Wiki read: `company/overview.md`, `protocols/handoffs.md`, `protocols/ordered-delegation.md`, `rules/capacity-levers.md`, `rules/customer-notices.md`.
- Rule taken from wiki: for a known absence of several days, temporary workers first, overtime only for any gap that remains; simulate combinations before proposing.
- What-if results: 2 temp workers for 2026-10-12..2026-10-23 would reduce KPI to 0 late orders and cost EUR 5,200; 4 temp workers would also reduce KPI to 0 late orders and cost EUR 10,400; 4 temp workers plus overtime would still end at 0 late orders but cost EUR 24,400.

# Steps
1. Book temporary workers for F-SOUTH: `erp__request_temp_workers(factory="F-SOUTH", count=2, from="2026-10-12", to="2026-10-23")`. Expected effect: restore enough staffing to cover the absence period with the lowest simulated cost. Expected cost: EUR 5,200.
2. Ask Cora to adjust the F-SOUTH schedule after the staffing change, using the approved KPI-safe result and the affected order ids `PRD-4203`, `PRD-4205`, `PRD-4207`, `PRD-4209`, `PRD-4211`, `PRD-4213`, `PRD-4215`. She must return the updated completion and delivery dates and confirm which orders remain late.
3. Ask Horst to inform only the customers whose promises remain broken after Cora’s update, using the ERP delivery dates he is given. He must return which customers were told and which dates were recorded in the CRM.
4. If the approved execution changes the KPI or reveals a need for broader follow-up, update the company wiki at the end of execution with durable lessons only; do not record live dates or stock.

# Outputs
- `.agent/plans/task-01M61E5E3BR5DWZW3NF1VT4SCW.md`
- `.agent/summaries/task-01M61E5E3BR5DWZW3NF1VT4SCW_plan_1.md`

# Risks and open questions
- The simulation shows 2 temp workers is enough in this case, but Cora may still keep some orders late if the downstream queue cannot be fully absorbed; that must be verified in execution.
- Horst can only notify customers after Cora returns ERP-confirmed delivery dates.
- Approval needed: whether to proceed with the lower-cost 2-worker package or request the larger staffing package despite the higher cost.

# Goal
Replan Werk Süd after the approved staffing change without making the KPI worse. Preserve the current priorities unless a change is required, and return the affected orders, their latest ERP completion and delivery dates, and which orders are still late.

# Inputs
- ERP overview date: `2026-10-05`.
- F-SOUTH has two absences: Lena Hartmann and Tobias Klein, both out from `2026-10-12` to `2026-10-23`.
- Max already booked 2 temporary workers for F-SOUTH for the same range.
- F-SOUTH capacity is `40` sofas/day through `2026-10-09`, then `30` sofas/day from `2026-10-12` to `2026-10-23` because the temp workers only partly offset the absences.
- F-SOUTH production orders concerned: `PRD-4203`, `PRD-4205`, `PRD-4207`, `PRD-4209`, `PRD-4211`, `PRD-4213`, `PRD-4215`.
- Current ERP late-order KPI for F-SOUTH is already clean: `lateOrders=0`, `sofasLate=0`, `lateOrdersCustomerNotInformed=0`.
- What-if checks show reprioritizing `PRD-4203` to priority `4` makes the KPI worse: `lateOrders 0 -> 1`, `sofasLate 0 -> 120`.
- What-if checks show moving `PRD-4203` to `F-NORTH` at priority `6` also makes the KPI worse: `lateOrders 0 -> 1`, `sofasLate 0 -> 150`.
- What-if checks show reprioritizing `PRD-4203` and `PRD-4205` together still makes the KPI worse: `lateOrders 0 -> 1`, `sofasLate 0 -> 120`.
- Wiki: `wiki/index.md` (catalogue), `wiki/lessons/autumn-bundle-late-even-with-capacity.md` (healthy queues can still fail after an unplanned bundle, so verify KPI after any change), `wiki/lessons/north-replan-spindle-motor.md` (only move work when it improves the KPI), `wiki/index.md` from the company wiki, plus `protocols/handoffs.md`, `protocols/ordered-delegation.md`, and `rules/capacity-levers.md` (capacity changes must be chosen by KPI and simulated first).

# Steps
1. Keep the existing priorities for `PRD-4203`, `PRD-4205`, `PRD-4207`, `PRD-4209`, `PRD-4211`, `PRD-4213`, and `PRD-4215`; do not apply a production-order change because the tested alternatives worsen the KPI.
2. In the execute step, re-read the F-SOUTH production orders from ERP and return the current completion and expected delivery dates for the seven named orders, plus the final list of late F-SOUTH orders.
3. If the ERP still shows zero late orders, report that no reprioritisation was required and that the staffing change was absorbed without schedule changes.

# Outputs
- `.agent/plans/task-a2a-4dfd174a-597f-4e00-b717-b10325a071c4.md`
- `.agent/summaries/task-a2a-4dfd174a-597f-4e00-b717-b10325a071c4_plan_1.md`

# Risks and open questions
- The current South queue is already on time, so any unnecessary move would create new lateness.
- The temp workers restore only part of the absent capacity; if a later change adds work to F-SOUTH, the queue may need another re-check.
- Open question for approval: should the execute step be limited to verification only, since every tested schedule change worsened the KPI?
